summary:
LUNA-01: Mission Control is an interactive space mission simulation game that puts players in the role of a Mission Director responsible for planning and executing a robotic mission to the Moon.

Players design their spacecraft, select scientific instruments, choose a lunar destination, and make critical decisions while managing limited budgets, mass, fuel, power, and mission risks. As the mission progresses, they encounter unexpected hazards, conduct lunar surveys, and work to transmit their scientific findings back to Earth. The experience is supported by real NASA datasets covering lunar environments, surface regions, lunar dust, and Earth–Moon orbital information.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning the complex trade-offs involved in space mission design into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. Rather than simply reading about mission planning, players can experiment, make mistakes, and see the consequences of their decisions. We hope to make space engineering more engaging and help students understand how science, technology, and engineering come together in a real mission.
details:
LUNA-01: Mission Control is an interactive, browser-based space mission simulation game that puts players in the role of a Mission Director responsible for planning and executing a robotic lunar science mission.

Players begin by selecting one of five lunar survey regions and designing their spacecraft. They must choose a launch vehicle, power system, scientific instrument, and protection kit while balancing limited resources such as budget, mass, fuel, and power. As the mission progresses, they choose a travel strategy and lunar orbit, conduct scientific surveys, respond to unexpected hazards, manage a lunar-night power crisis, and make decisions about transmitting their findings back to Earth. Each decision affects the mission outcome, which is explained in a final mission report.

The game incorporates four curated NASA-based datasets containing 91 records covering lunar environments, surface regions, lunar dust, and Earth–Moon orbital information. Scientific values retain their sources, units, and confidence labels, while simplified gameplay calculations are clearly identified as game models.

We developed LUNA-01 using HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas 2D, and the Web Audio API. Its planetary visuals, animations, spacecraft, and sound effects are generated procedurally, without external image or audio files.

Our creative approach is to make scientific information part of the gameplay rather than simply presenting it as background reading. We considered engineering trade-offs, scientific reliability, resource limitations, mission risks, communication, and gameplay balance. Our aim is to make space mission engineering more approachable and engaging, especially for students who rarely get to experiment with the decisions behind a real space mission.
